scope.q: What is the acceptable latency for a field technician to receive an accurate part recommendation, and what are the specific consequences of a wrong recommendation?
scope.why: Understanding the performance requirements and the cost of error will guide the choice of retrieval methods, validation steps, and overall system architecture.

scope.q: Beyond 'which part fits which unit,' are there other types of queries or relationships technicians need, such as compatibility with other parts, installation instructions, or common troubleshooting tips?
scope.why: Clarifying the full range of desired information retrieval will define the scope of data extraction and the complexity of the underlying knowledge model.

scope.q: Are there existing digital indices, part numbers, or unit identifiers in any system that can be cross-referenced or used as a 'ground truth' to validate information extracted from the scanned PDFs?
scope.why: Leveraging any structured data would significantly reduce the reliance on potentially error-prone OCR and information extraction from unstructured text.

decomposition.title: Document Ingestion & OCR Pipeline
decomposition.why: Converting thousands of scanned PDFs into machine-readable text is the foundational step for any further processing.

decomposition.title: Information Extraction & Structuring
decomposition.why: Identifying and extracting key entities like units, parts, and their relationships from raw text is crucial for building a queryable knowledge base.

decomposition.title: Knowledge Graph Construction & Persistence
decomposition.why: Storing the extracted, structured data in a robust, query-optimized format is necessary for efficient retrieval and complex relationship queries.

decomposition.title: Natural Language Query & Retrieval Service
decomposition.why: Enabling field technicians to ask questions in plain language and receive relevant answers requires a robust interface and search logic.

decomposition.title: Human-in-the-Loop Validation & Feedback System
decomposition.why: Given the potential for OCR and extraction errors, a mechanism for human review and continuous improvement is essential for accuracy and trust.

components.name: OCR Processor Service
components.sub: Converts scanned images into searchable text.

components.name: Document Store
components.sub: Stores raw PDFs and OCR'd text.

components.name: LLM Coordinator
components.sub: Interprets natural language, queries KG, formats answers.

components.name: Feedback & Validation UI
components.sub: Allows human review and correction of extracted data.

sprint.title: Core OCR & Document Ingestion
sprint.deliv: OCR pipeline processing 100 sample PDFs with text output stored in Document Store, basic error logging.

sprint.title: Initial Information Extraction Model
sprint.deliv: Prototype extraction agent identifying 'Unit' and 'Part' entities from sample OCR text, outputting JSON relations.

sprint.title: Knowledge Graph MVP & Population
sprint.deliv: Knowledge graph schema defined and populated with extracted data from 50 sample documents, queryable via programmatic API.

sprint.title: Basic Query API & Field Tech UI
sprint.deliv: Frontend UI allowing text input and displaying hardcoded responses; backend API receiving queries and returning dummy data.

sprint.title: NLQ Integration with Knowledge Graph
sprint.deliv: End-to-end flow: Tech UI query -> LLM Coordinator -> KG query -> formatted answer displayed in UI for a few specific part-unit questions.

sprint.title: Human-in-the-Loop Feedback Prototype
sprint.deliv: Admin UI allowing review and correction of 10 extracted relationships, with updates reflected in the Knowledge Graph.

sprint.title: Pilot Demo & Metrics
sprint.deliv: Live demonstration of the end-to-end system with 20 key unit-part queries, presenting initial accuracy and latency metrics.

risks.risk: Low OCR accuracy on older, low-resolution scanned PDFs leading to missing or incorrect entity extraction.
risks.mitigation: Implement a tiered OCR strategy, using advanced models for poor quality scans and a human-in-the-loop validation step for entities with low confidence scores.

risks.risk: Inconsistent naming conventions or ambiguous descriptions across thousands of manuals making entity resolution difficult.
risks.mitigation: Develop a canonical entity mapping service, leveraging fuzzy matching and potentially an LLM to normalize part/unit names, with a dedicated review process for high-ambiguity cases.

risks.risk: Scalability issues when processing thousands of large PDF files, leading to excessively long ingestion times.
risks.mitigation: Design a distributed, parallel processing pipeline for OCR and extraction, prioritizing high-demand manuals first, and implementing robust retry mechanisms.

risks.risk: Field tech adoption is low due to perceived inaccuracy or slow response times of the system.
risks.mitigation: Conduct early and frequent user testing with field techs, incorporating their feedback directly into UI/UX and relevance tuning, and providing clear confidence scores with answers.
